title: Unveiling the antiviral inhibitory activity of ebselen and ebsulfur derivatives on SARS-CoV-2 using machine learning-bas

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines pIC₅₀ as "pIC₅₀ = (1 / IC₅₀ (M))". pIC₅₀ conventionally means −log10(IC₅₀ in molar units), not the reciprocal concentration. The stated formula produces values with inverse-molar units and radically changes both scale and ordering/interpretation of all QSAR targets and predictions.

Eq. (4) defines R² as Σ(y_pred−ȳ)² / Σ(y_exp−ȳ)². This is not the coefficient of determination for predictions. Predictive R² is ordinarily 1−Σ(y_exp−y_pred)²/Σ(y_exp−ȳ)² (or, if explicitly intended, the squared correlation between observed and predicted values). The supplied expression can reward predictions that are far from observations and therefore invalidates the stated interpretation of reported R² values as goodness of fit.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract versus QSAR Results and final Conclusion
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract reports training R² values of 0.83, 0.82, and 0.92 and test RMSE values of 0.27, 0.18, and 0.09 for MLR, RF, and ANN, respectively. The Results instead report MLR training R²=0.69 and test RMSE=0.56, RF R²=0.82 and test RMSE=0.18, and ANN R²=0.89 and test RMSE=0.05. The final paragraph repeats ANN R²=0.89 and test RMSE=0.05. These are material contradictions in the core model-performance claims.

The RF grid says that "Min samples split" was tested at "1, 2, 3." In scikit-learn RandomForestRegressor, min_samples_split must be an integer at least 2; a value of 1 is invalid and raises a parameter-validation error. Thus the reported grid cannot have been run as described.

predicted_errors.error_location: RF hyperparameter-selection description immediately before Table 1(a) versus Table 1(a) and reported best RF model
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says optimization varied four parameters including "Max feature," min_sample_leaf, min_samples_split, and number of estimators. Table 1(a), however, omits max_features entirely and instead lists max_depth. The Results then claim the best model had "a max feature of 4." Since the tested max_features values are not reported and max_depth is not included in the preceding list of varied parameters, the described search space is internally inconsistent and not reproducible.

predicted_errors.error_location: Cytotoxicity-methods paragraph: "evaluated according to the previous description³⁶"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reference 36 is already cited earlier as one of the Kennard–Stone algorithm references: "Kennard–Stone³⁵,³⁶ algorithm." It therefore cannot simultaneously be the cited prior description for the Vero E6/CellTiter 96 cytotoxicity protocol. The cytotoxicity-method citation is misnumbered or misattributed.

The paper says, "Seven ebselen analogs were tested against four strains of SARS-CoV-2 Mᵖʳᵒ," but the actual protocol identifies only one virus, SARS-CoV-2 B.1.617.2 (Delta; ON381169), and describes infection with that virus. Moreover, Mᵖʳᵒ is a viral protease, not a SARS-CoV-2 strain. The number and identity of tested viral strains must be corrected.

predicted_errors.error_location: LB-PaCS-MD methods and subsequent binding-pathway claim
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The method explicitly describes LB-PaCS-MD as focused on "ligand-unbinding states" and says snapshots are ranked by the ligand–C145 COM distance for subsequent cycles. It then places P8 about 30 Å from C145 and claims to sample a binding pathway into the active site. An unbinding-oriented selection protocol cannot drive association from a distant ligand unless selection is explicitly reversed (selecting decreasing distances); neither a reversed criterion nor its implementation is reported. The claimed binding path is therefore not supported by the method as described.

The receptor is stated to be the "3D structure of ebselen covalently bound dimeric SARS-CoV-2 Mᵖʳᵒ (PDB ID: 7BAK)," after which P8 is placed far from C145. The text never states that the covalently bound ebselen was removed or that C145 was restored to an unmodified receptor. If 7BAK was used as stated, the active site is occupied/modified by ebselen and cannot represent an unbound receptor for P8 association. This essential preparation step must be specified and corrected.

The paper first states that P8 orients "the Se of the benzoselenazole moiety toward the S of C145" and defines the free-energy coordinate as S(C145)–Se(P8). It then claims a "chalcogen-bonding interaction between S atoms in P8 and C145." These are incompatible descriptions of the stated binding contact: the proposed chalcogen atom is selenium, not an S atom in P8.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Results paragraph interpreting Fig. 6A–C
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: P8 is called the "most potent inhibitor" and a "good potential candidate," yet the reported 100-µM enzyme result is residual enzymatic activity of 64.5%, i.e. only 35.5% inhibition at a very high concentration. The live-virus results for P8 are explicitly non-monotonic, with inhibition reduced at higher concentrations because crystals/solubility problems were observed, and no P8 EC₅₀ is reported despite the methods claiming EC₅₀ calculation. These observations do not substantiate a potency or antiviral-candidate conclusion without qualified language and concentration-response/solubility-corrected data.
